A twenty-one year old bodybuilder dies just after one a.m., poisoned by his own fat burner.
And the authorities already knew what he'd bought.
Jack Napman wants to lose weight for bodybuilding. Online, he finds a fat burner called D N P.
Over two days, he takes a lot of it.
Every gym has someone with a secret fat burner from a guy online.
Then the toxicity hits. Hospital. Cardiac arrest.
Wait. What exactly was he taking?

You see, D N P isn't a supplement. It's an industrial chemical, used in dyes, fertiliser... and explosives. It makes your body burn fuel as pure heat, like a stove stuck on full, with no off switch. And there's no specific antidote.
Doctors gave it to patients in the nineteen thirties. America banned it in nineteen thirty-eight.
And those authorities? They'd spotted Jack's purchase. Their warning letter was delayed.
In twenty twenty-two, a coroner says D N P should never be used for human consumption. And as long as it's sold online, the risk remains.
So should selling it be treated like dealing drugs?
A fat burner that was never meant for people at all.
